name: Cross-body stretch
movement: one arm drawn across the chest with the other hand and held

phone.placement: Stand the phone up on the floor, two or three metres away, facing you.

words.hint: Facing the phone, one arm drawn across the chest with the other hand, held.
words.start: Stand the phone up on the floor. Stand facing it, draw one arm across your chest with the other hand, and hold.
words.position: Stand facing the phone. Bring the stiff arm across your chest and use the other hand above the elbow to draw it gently further, until a stretch is felt at the back of the shoulder.
words.top: The hand drawn across to the far shoulder, the shoulders level and the chest still facing the phone, held.
howto: Stand facing the phone. Lift the stiff arm to about chest height and bring it across your body.
With the other hand above the elbow, draw it gently further across until you feel the stretch at the back of the shoulder.
Hold for the count. Shoulders level — don’t let the stretching shoulder hike up — and the chest facing the phone.
words.cannot: How strong the stretch feels: it sees the hand across the chest, the shoulders level and the chest facing the phone.
words.about: Cross-body stretch — facing the phone: the reach, as the wrist-to-far-shoulder distance against the trunk, at most 45% (the hand at or past the far shoulder); the stretching shoulder within 10° of level with the other, since it hikes up under the pull; and the chest facing the phone, as the shoulder width at least 80% of its width at the start. The clock runs while all three are right. Twenty seconds a hold, three holds.
words.lost: Stand facing the camera, both arms in the picture
words.hold: That is it — hold the stretch
words.safety: A pull at the back of the shoulder, not a pinch at the front. Ease off if it pinches.
words.harder: A longer hold; a little more draw across.
words.mistakes: Pulling at the elbow joint rather than above it; the shoulder hiking up; turning the body toward the arm instead of drawing it across.

measurements.label: hand from the far shoulder, % of trunk
measurements.why: The wrist-to-far-shoulder distance against the trunk: the hand across at the far shoulder reads under 45; an arm hanging by the side reads over 100.

settings.label: Hand from the far shoulder, % of the trunk, at most

measurements.label: how far across
measurements.why: The reach the other way up, so the arm across the chest is the larger of the two sides and is the one measured.

measurements.label: shoulder above the other
measurements.why: The shoulder line off level: the stretching shoulder hikes up under the pull.

measurements.label: shoulder width, % of start
measurements.why: The shoulder width against the hips, as a percent of its width at the start: turning toward the arm narrows it.

settings.label: Shoulder width, % of the start, at least

faults.label: Draw further
faults.text: Draw the arm further across, to the far shoulder
faults.deep: Use the other hand above the elbow to bring it across

faults.label: Shoulder hiking
faults.text: Shoulder down — level with the other

faults.label: Body turning
faults.text: Keep the chest facing the phone — draw the arm across, don’t turn
